def: Electricity is the set of physical phenomena associated with the presence and motion of matter possessing an electric charge.

c: And in the 20th century, new discoveries in genetics and physics laid the foundations for new sub disciplines such as molecular biology and particle physics.
def: Physics is the scientific study of matter, its fundamental constituents, its motion and behavior through space and time, and the related entities of energy and force.

c: He also devised one of the most important methods in preventive medicine, when in 1880 he produced a vaccine against rabies.
def: A vaccine is a biological preparation that provides active acquired immunity to a particular infectious or malignant disease.

c: Equally important in the rise of ecology, however, were microbiology and soil science—particularly the cycle of life concept, prominent in the work of Louis Pasteur and Ferdinand Cohn.
def: Microbiology is the scientific study of microorganisms, those being of unicellular (single-celled), multicellular, or acellular.

def: In physics and chemistry, the law of conservation of mass or principle of mass conservation states that for any system which is closed to all incoming and outgoing transfers of matter, the mass of the system must remain constant over time.

c: Neuroscience began to be recognized as a distinct academic discipline in its own right.
def: Neuroscience is the scientific study of the nervous system, its functions, and its disorders.

c: Scientific scholarship during the Byzantine Empire played an important role in the transmission of classical knowledge to the Islamic world and to Renaissance Italy, and also in the transmission of…
def: Scientific scholarship during the Byzantine Empire played an important role in the transmission of classical knowledge to the Islamic world and to Renaissance Italy, and also in the transmission of Islamic science to Renaissance Italy.

c: Science in the Renaissance was predominantly an extension of medieval traditions of natural philosophy but also included a radical revolution in the European understanding of the Earth's geography…
def: Science in the Renaissance was predominantly an extension of medieval traditions of natural philosophy but also included a radical revolution in the European understanding of the Earth's geography and produced new ideas and methods in anatomy, mathematics, and astronomy.

def: Vitalism is an idea that living organisms are differentiated from the non-living by the presence of forces, properties or powers including those which may not be physical or chemical.

c: Pasteur invented the process of pasteurization, to help prevent the spread of disease through milk and other foods.
def: In food processing, pasteurization (-isation) is a process of food preservation in which packaged foods are treated with mild heat, usually to less than 100 °C (212 °F), to eliminate pathogens and extend shelf life.

c: Advances in synthetic biology with computer assistance led to the creation of artificial microbial life, such as JCVI-syn3.0 in 2016 and xenobots in 2020.
def: Synthetic biology (SynBio) is a multidisciplinary scientific field that applies the principles of engineering to develop new biological parts, devices, and systems or to redesign existing systems found in nature.

c: The relationship between science and religion has been variously characterized in terms of "conflict", "harmony", "complexity", and "mutual independence", among others.
def: The relationship between science and religion involves discussions that interconnect the study of the natural world, history, philosophy, and theology.

def: In the history of ideas, the continuity thesis is the hypothesis that there was no radical discontinuity between the intellectual development of the Middle Ages and the developments in the Renaissance and early modern period.

def: Divination is the attempt to gain insight into a question or situation by way of a magic ritual or practice.

c: Thus, in addition to medicine, therapies included prayer, incantation, and ritual.
def: An incantation, spell, charm, enchantment, or bewitchery is a magical formula intended to trigger a magical effect on a person or objects.

c: The Fall of Constantinople in 1453 caused many Byzantine scholars to seek refuge in the West.
def: The migration waves of Byzantine Greek scholars and émigrés in the period following the end of the Byzantine Empire in 1453 are considered by many scholars key to the revival of Greek studies that led to the development of Renaissance humanism and science.
